ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory screening of all general partners, limited partners, UBOs, authorized signatories and material counterparties against the OFAC SDN List, UN Security Council Consolidated List, UK Sanctions List (OFSI), Bermuda Sanctions List, EU Consolidated List, and Interpol notices. Enhanced due diligence is required for foreign PEPs, domestic PEPs, and international organization PEPs per FATF Recommendation 12 and the Proceeds of Crime (AML/ATF) Regulations 1998. For the Swift_TT and Escrow_Inspection_Wire payment rails, independent verification of source of funds, trading documentation, and beneficial ownership is required; elevated scrutiny applies to transfers involving high-risk jurisdictions or high-value portable goods (SSD/CPU).

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Bermuda Companies Registry e-Registry (Registrar of Companies, Ministry of Finance, Government of Bermuda)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: English exclusively; an exempted partnership name must end with the statutory suffix 'Limited Partnership' or the abbreviation 'L.P.'; names in non-Latin scripts must be transliterated into the Latin alphabet for registration; Bermuda does not register parallel foreign-script names; the name must not be identical or misleadingly similar to an existing Bermuda registered entity or reserved name.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: A name rejection is recorded in the Registry and the rejected name cannot be reserved unless materially amended. The applicant may file a written request for reconsideration with the Registrar of Companies within 14 calendar days, supported by legal submissions and evidence of distinctiveness. If the Registrar maintains the refusal, the applicant may seek administrative review by the Minister of Finance, with residual recourse to judicial review before the Supreme Court of Bermuda. An amended name may be re-submitted immediately without prejudice; each new reservation triggers a new statutory fee.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: A physical registered office in Bermuda is mandatory under the Exempted Partnerships Act 1992, s. 6; a P.O. Box or virtual office is not acceptable as the statutory registered office. The registered office function is typically supplied by a licensed corporate services provider. Trading, management, and administrative functions may be conducted remotely from outside Bermuda, but the Economic Substance Amendment Act 2019 requires an annual economic substance declaration. The declared open-market brokerage model (third-party spot trading of SSD and CPU, non-group transactions) is likely outside the scope of 'distribution and service centre business' as defined under the Economic Substance Act 2018, which is limited to intra-group distribution; the declaration must nevertheless be filed in all cases, and the ELP must state whether it is tax resident in Bermuda or another jurisdiction. If management and control are exercised from the UK, UK tax residence and transparency rules may apply to the partners.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Low — estimated 2% to 5% per annum for a non-regulated ELP maintaining a serviced registered office. The Registrar of Companies may conduct verification of registered office existence and adequacy; the Bermuda Monetary Authority and the Financial Intelligence Agency may schedule AML/CFT inspections of the licensed corporate services provider. Unannounced physical inspection of partner premises is unlikely where all partners operate outside Bermuda.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Exempted Limited Partnerships Act 2009 (Bermuda), ss. 4-5 (Application and Registration), s. 7 (Certificate of Registration), s. 9 (Registered Office), s. 12 (Execution of Documents); read with the Companies Act 1981 Part XI, the Beneficial Ownership (Exempted Limited Partnerships) Regulations 2018, and the Economic Substance Act 2018.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Registrar of Companies, Corporate Registry, Ministry of Finance, Government of Bermuda; online portal BERMUDABusiness; counter at 4th Floor, Government Administration Building, 133 Front Street, Hamilton HM 12.
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Application for Registration of an Exempted Limited Partnership (Form ELP1), accompanied by the executed Exempted Limited Partnership Agreement, the Statutory Declaration of the General Partner, and the Consent of the Resident Representative; completion evidenced by a Certificate of Registration.
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum capital and no escrow account requirement apply to a Bermuda Exempted Limited Partnership; capital contribution levels are fixed solely in the Limited Partnership Agreement, and the General Partner's statutory declaration confirms that at least one General Partner and one Limited Partner have subscribed to the partnership.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: EXEMPTED LIMITED PARTNERSHIP - RESOLUTION OF THE GENERAL PARTNER. 1. RESOLVED that the General Partner approves the initial subscription of partnership interests and the capital contributions set out in the Exempted Limited Partnership Agreement. 2. RESOLVED that the registered office of the Partnership be established at the address of the licensed registered office provider in Hamilton, Bermuda, and that the resident representative be appointed. 3. RESOLVED that the following officers be appointed with authority to open bank and escrow accounts, execute purchase and sale contracts for SSD and server processor transactions, and issue payment instructions: Managing Officer; Compliance Officer. 4. RESOLVED that the General Partner's signatories be authorized to file the Application for Registration, pay the registration fee, and effect all ancillary acts.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registrar of Companies, Corporate Registry, Bermuda via BERMUDABusiness online portal
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Conduct a corporate name availability search through the Corporate Registry to confirm that the proposed name does not conflict with existing registered names or contain restricted words implying Crown connection or regulated financial activity. Submit a Name Reservation Form (Form NR), together with a certified copy of the corporate General Partner's board resolution and notarized KYC identification of the General Partner. The reserved name must end with 'Limited Partnership' or 'L.P.'.
required_dossiers: Completed Name Reservation Form (Form NR)
Certified copy of corporate General Partner's board resolution approving the proposed name
Certificate of Good Standing for the corporate General Partner
Notarized KYC identification pack for the General Partner and intended Limited Partners
Statement of intended activities and exempted status declaration
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name is refused or challenged by the Registrar, the applicant may file a written submission with supporting evidence of no conflict within 14 days, or reserve an alternative name; a contested decision may be escalated to a hearing before the Registrar of Companies.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Drafting and Notarization of the Limited Partnership Agreement
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Notary Public and corporate legal counsel in conjunction with the Corporate Registry, Bermuda
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Draft the Exempted Limited Partnership Agreement (ELPA), the Application for Registration (Form ELP1), and the Statutory Declaration of the General Partner. The ELPA must state the name, nature of business, registered office in Bermuda, identity of General and Limited Partners, capital contribution schedule, profit and loss sharing ratios, management powers, and dissolution events. Execute the documents before a notary public; where the General Partner is a corporation, execution must be accompanied by a certified extract of its board resolution and incumbency certificate.
required_dossiers: Draft Exempted Limited Partnership Agreement (ELPA)
Form ELP1 Application for Registration
Statutory Declaration of the General Partner
Consent to act as Resident Representative executed by a licensed registered office provider
Certified copy of corporate General Partner's board resolution and incumbency certificate
Notarized KYC/AML wallet for each partner including source of funds declaration
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Registrar issues a requisition letter identifying defects in the ELPA or declarations, the applicant may file corrective amendments to the ELPA and re-executed statutory declarations within 21 days to avoid automatic refusal under section 6 of the Exempted Limited Partnerships Act 2009.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Statutory Filing and Issuance of the Certificate of Registration
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registrar of Companies, Corporate Registry, Ministry of Finance, Bermuda (BERMUDABusiness online portal or counter submission)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: File the executed Form ELP1, the ELPA, the Statutory Declaration, the resident representative's consent, and the registered office confirmation through the BERMUDABusiness portal or in person at the Corporate Registry. Pay the statutory registration fee of USD 1,780 by bank transfer or electronic payment. Upon satisfactory review, the Registrar issues a Certificate of Registration for the Exempted Limited Partnership, which is conclusive evidence of formation and legal personality.
required_dossiers: Executed Form ELP1 Application for Registration
Executed Exempted Limited Partnership Agreement
Original Statutory Declaration of the General Partner
Original Consent of the Resident Representative
Registered office address confirmation from a licensed service provider
Payment confirmation of the statutory filing fee
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the application is queried, counsel may file an amended application or supplementary declarations within 14 days of the requisition; the corrected submission is reviewed within 3 business days. Persistent non-compliance may be cured by re-filing under section 5 and paying an additional administrative fee.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Post-Registration Governance, Registered Office, and Bank Account Activation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Bermuda Monetary Authority licensed banks and electronic money institutions; licensed corporate service providers; Registrar of Companies for Beneficial Ownership filing
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Activate the registered office and resident representative arrangement with a licensed exempted undertakings service provider. Convene the first meeting of the General Partner to ratify capital subscriptions, adopt the AML/ATF compliance framework consistent with the BMA AML/ATF Guidance Notes, and appoint the Managing Officer and Compliance Officer. Submit the Beneficial Ownership Return (Form BO) under the Beneficial Ownership (Exempted Limited Partnerships) Regulations 2018. Open operating bank and escrow inspection wire payment accounts with a BMA licensed bank or EMI; provision the medium-risk Enhanced Due Diligence pack, including source of wealth for semiconductor trading operations.
required_dossiers: Certificate of Registration of the Exempted Limited Partnership
BMA-compliant KYC/AML pack for all partners and beneficial owners
Beneficial Ownership Return (Form BO) filed with the Registrar
AML/ATF compliance manual and enterprise risk assessment
Registered office and resident representative service agreement
Bank and escrow account application forms for Swift TT and Escrow Inspection Wire rails
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the first bank or EMI declines onboarding, re-apply to a second-tier Bermudian licensed institution or a UK electronic money institution under a Bermuda gateway structure, accompanied by an enhanced source-of-funds analysis for spot semiconductor brokerage; the Beneficial Ownership filing may be internally remediated within 30 days by submitting a rectification return to the Registrar.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Economic Substance, Annual Return, and Tax Status Admission
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registrar of Companies (Annual Return and Economic Substance declaration); Office of the Tax Commissioner, Bermuda (Payroll Tax registration); HMRC for UK partner-level reporting
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Register for Bermuda payroll tax with the Office of the Tax Commissioner if the partnership employs staff in Bermuda. File the Annual ELP Return with the Registrar of Companies. Submit the annual Economic Substance declaration under the Economic Substance Act 2018; for an ELP managed and controlled from the United Kingdom, claim the non-resident entity exclusion on the basis of UK tax residence and file supporting evidence. Coordinate partner-level pass-through reporting to HMRC in accordance with UK partnership taxation rules.
required_dossiers: Annual ELP Return (Form ELP-AR) filed with the Registrar of Companies
Economic Substance declaration or non-resident exclusion evidence under the Economic Substance Act 2018
Payroll tax registration certificate (if Bermuda employees are engaged)
UK partner-level tax filings and HMRC partnership statements
Statutory audit report if gross assets exceed the Bermuda audit threshold
Certificate of Good Standing issued by the Registrar
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Late filing penalties may be mitigated by submitting the overdue returns with an explanatory letter and applying in writing to the Registrar for administrative penalty waiver; economic substance sanctions may be cured by demonstrating UK tax residence through double tax treaty residency certificates and HMRC correspondence within 30 days of notice.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Not applicable - no industrial or manufacturing license is required for open-market wholesale brokerage of SSDs and server processors. Should physical premises be occupied in Bermuda, the Department of Planning, Ministry of Home Affairs, would administer use-of-premises certification and permitting.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Not applicable - no statutory business license applies to an offshore exempted limited partnership engaged in wholesale semiconductor brokerage; no Department of Licensing endorsement is required for this commercial activity.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Department of Environment and Natural Resources, Government of Bermuda
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt - office-only wholesale brokerage with no manufacturing, effluent, or emissions-generating processes; no Environmental Impact Assessment required; administrative registration only in the event of future warehouse leasing.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Not triggered by current scope. If warehousing is added, effluent discharged to Bermuda Government sewers must comply with Water Resources Act 1975 consent limits (BOD below 20 mg/l, suspended solids below 30 mg/l); standby generator VOC and combustion emissions must meet Clean Air Act 1991 best practicable means thresholds; transboundary movement of defective or end-of-life electronic equipment must comply with the Waste Management Act and Basel Convention prior notification and consent procedures.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire safety certification from the Bermuda Fire and Rescue Service for any occupied office, including means of escape and emergency lighting compliance; structural load inspection certification for any storage area exceeding 50 kg/m2 rated capacity; workplace clearance under Bermuda occupational health and safety regulations, including electrical safety, fire drill records, first aid provision, and a written emergency evacuation plan.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Office of the Tax Commissioner, Ministry of Finance, Government of Bermuda (national tax authority administering payroll tax and the Corporate Income Tax Act 2023); Registrar of Companies, Bermuda Registry, Ministry of Finance (entity registration and statutory partnership identifier); Bermuda Customs Service, Ministry of Finance (customs duty and transit/re-export clearance); official e-services portal: www.gov.bm.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: Step 1 - Register the Exempted Limited Partnership with the Registrar of Companies under the Exempted Partnerships Act 1992; the issued Certificate of Registration and registration number serve as the ELP's primary statutory and tax reference because Bermuda does not issue a separate TIN for exempted partnerships. Step 2 - Register with the Office of the Tax Commissioner for payroll tax only if the ELP employs individuals working in Bermuda. Step 3 - Register for Corporate Income Tax (CIT) with the Office of the Tax Commissioner only if the ELP is a constituent entity of an MNE group with consolidated annual revenue of EUR 750 million or more; otherwise no CIT registration is required. Step 4 - Obtain a customs declarant code from the Bermuda Customs Service if the ELP imports, exports, or transships goods through Bermuda. A foreign entity with no Bermuda employees, no Bermuda premises, and no MNE-group CIT exposure has no mandatory Bermuda tax registration and may evidence its status by its Certificate of Registration and an optional tax assurance letter from the Ministry of Finance.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: Bermuda has no check-the-box or hybrid mismatch election regime. An ELP is fiscally transparent and tax-neutral in Bermuda (general income tax rate of 0%), so classification elections are only relevant under the Corporate Income Tax Act 2023 for in-scope MNE groups. Available elections include: (i) single-filing election whereby the Bermuda ultimate parent entity submits a consolidated CIT return for Bermuda constituent entities; (ii) irrevocable election to apply the Qualifying Domestic Minimum Top-Up Tax (QDMTT) before foreign parent jurisdictions; (iii) exclusion elections for governmental, non-profit, pension, and international shipping entities; and (iv) OECD Pillar Two administrative elections for investment entities, offshore/onshore pooling, and safe harbour relief consistent with the OECD Agreed Administrative Guidance.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: No VAT, GST, or sales and use tax exists in Bermuda. As a British Overseas Territory, Bermuda sits outside the UK VAT area, so a Bermudian ELP has no UK VAT registration obligation absent a UK-established presence or a UK-nexus taxable supply. Bermuda's only indirect tax is customs import duty imposed by the Customs Tariff Act 1965, chargeable exclusively on goods entering Bermuda for local consumption; exports, transit, and re-exports are not subject to duty.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: N/A in BMD - Bermuda levies no VAT/GST, so no local-currency turnover threshold triggers indirect tax registration. A customs declarant code is required per importer of record regardless of annual import value.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Bermuda does not mandate real-time fiscal e-invoicing, continuous transaction controls (CTC), API-based clearance, or digital stamping for B2B wholesale or brokerage transactions. Import and export/transit declarations must be filed electronically through the Bermuda Customs single-window e-Declaration system; clearance occurs upon accepted declaration, duty payment or security, and any risk-flagged physical inspection. No electronic invoice clearance is required for spot semiconductor trades.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Not applicable - Bermuda has no VAT/GST, so there is no export VAT zero-rating claim, no refund mechanism, and no statutory export-rate certificate to obtain. SSDs and server CPUs exported from or transshipped through Bermuda attract no Bermudian duty; traders must simply declare the goods as exports or goods in transit. For completeness, if the ELP were ever part of an in-scope MNE group (EUR 750M+ consolidated revenue), the 15% Bermuda CIT could reach offshore wholesale profit under OECD GloBE rules, but that is an income tax matter and carries no zero-rating or refund feature.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Bermuda Customs electronic export entry or transit/transshipment declaration
Bill of Lading or Air Waybill evidencing physical movement of SSD and CPU chips
Commercial invoice and detailed packing list
Certificate of Origin (when preferential or statistical treatment is claimed)
SWIFT MT103 / inward remittance evidence of export proceeds settlement, retained for the 180-day FX repatriation file
ELP Certificate of Registration and underlying trade documentation
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: No export VAT clawback exists because no VAT is chargeable. Customs misdeclarations, including false transit or re-export declarations, are penalized under the Customs Act 1965 and the Customs Tariff Act 1965 by fines, forfeiture of goods, and potential imprisonment on conviction. If the ELP becomes subject to the Corporate Income Tax Act 2023, the Tax Commissioner may invoke general anti-avoidance rules, recharacterize or disallow artificial export/transit structures, assess understated GloBE income, and impose penalties of up to 100% of the tax shortfall plus interest; knowingly false documents in a tax or customs return constitute criminal fraud offences.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Exempted Partnership Declaration (Annual Return) confirming registered office, general partner identity, and limited partner register status
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Registrar of Companies, Corporate Registry, Government of Bermuda
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: On or before 31 January each year for the preceding 12-month filing period; an anniversary-based cycle aligned with the ELP registration date is permitted by the Registrar
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing accrues standard Registrar penalty charges; continued non-filing over 6 months exposes the ELP to a published strike-off notice and administrative dissolution, with restoration subject to court order

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Exemption Fee / Annual Government Fee under the Exempted Partnerships Act 1992
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Registrar of Companies and Accountant General, Government of Bermuda
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Payable annually on or before the registration anniversary date (1 January for calendar-year registered partnerships); the tariff is published by the Ministry of Finance
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Non-payment cancels the partnership's exempted status, exposes the partnership and general partner to default penalties and interest, and leads to strike-off after formal demand

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Economic Substance Declaration (ESD) for distribution and service centre / wholesale trading activity
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Registrar of Companies (Bermuda Economic Substance Regime)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 6 months after the end of the financial year (30 June for a calendar-year ELP; 31 December for a June year-end ELP)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Default triggers exchange of information with EU member states and penalties assessed by the Bermuda Tax Authority, escalating to BMD 100,000 per offence for false or late filings

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Mandatory independent audit where gross annual revenue exceeds approximately US$5,000,000 or total assets exceed US$1,000,000, where the Partnership Agreement prescribes audit, or where the ELP consolidates into an IFRS group requiring audited financial statements; passive or sub-threshold spot-trading partnerships remain audit-exempt
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: IFRS as the statutory default; US GAAP is accepted for US-connected parent groups; Bermuda has no locally promulgated GAAP and permits a recognised international framework for foreign-controlled exempted partnerships

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: The General Partner must perform an annual UBO and AML/KYC refresh of every limited partner, record any transfer affecting 10% or more of partnership interests within 14 days, and confirm the beneficial ownership register to the Bermuda registered agent; a UBO confirmation notification is transmitted to the Registrar where the Bermuda Beneficial Ownership Secure Search (BOSS) regime applies to the ELP
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of Limited Partners and Capital Contributions
Register of General Partners and Control Rights
Register of Transfers of Partnership Interests

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: USD 1,800 - 4,500 per annum (Bermuda registered office, resident general partner/agent service and corporate secretarial filing support)
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 4,500 - 10,500 for a spot SSD/CPU wholesale ELP with transactional banking records; fee scale rises with volume, intercompany positions, and consolidation work

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 0% general corporate income tax; a 15% corporate income tax applies solely to constituent entities of multinational enterprise (MNE) groups with consolidated annual revenue ≥ EUR 750 million under the Corporate Income Tax Act 2023, effective for fiscal years beginning on or after 1 January 2025.
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Exempted Limited Partnerships (ELPs) are fiscally transparent; no entity-level tax arises on the ELP unless it falls within the Bermuda CIT scope as a constituent entity of an in-scope MNE group. No statutory tax holidays or preferential deductions exist; a potential Pillar Two top-up tax may apply at 15% if the ELP is part of a covered MNE group with low-taxed profits.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Form CIT-1 (Corporate Income Tax Return) – Bermuda Tax Administration Portal (TAP); for ELPs falling within CIT scope as a constituent entity of a covered MNE group.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Due by the last day of the fifteenth month following the end of the fiscal year (e.g., for a 31 December year-end, filing is due 31 March of the second subsequent year); quarterly estimated payments are required based on provisional CIT liabilities.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Entity identification: name, ELP registration number, tax residency status, and registered office in Bermuda.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Identify the ELP as an exempted partnership and state the direct and indirect owners (Partners) and their tax residences.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: MNE Group classification: confirm whether the ELP is a constituent entity of a group with revenue ≥ EUR 750M and designate the ultimate parent entity and its jurisdiction.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: A non-resident partner’s share information must be disclosed only if the ELP itself is required to file; otherwise the partnership is omitted.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Profit allocation and taxable income: computation of the ELP’s adjusted taxable income or loss, based on audited financial statements and the OECD GloBE Model Rules.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Allocate profits to partners according to the partnership agreement; a tax-transparent ELP generally passes income to partners without entity-level tax.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Effective tax rate (ETR) and top-up tax: report the ETR per jurisdiction and any additional top-up tax due under the Pillar Two rules.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: If the ELP has no taxable presence and is not part of a covered group, complete this box as N/A.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing: fixed penalty of BMD 500 per month up to BMD 5,000; in addition, a penalty of 5% of unpaid tax for the first month and 0.5% per subsequent month, capped at 25% of the tax due. Inaccurate return and negligence: penalty up to 100% of the tax underpaid; deliberate concealment: criminal prosecution and imprisonment up to 2 years. A company or partnership that fails to file an ESR may incur a penalty of BMD 100,000 for the first offence and BMD 250,000 for subsequent failures.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: ESR-1 (Economic Substance Return) – Bermuda Beneficial Ownership Secure Portal (BERS); mandatory for every registered exempted partnership under the Economic Substance Act 2018.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Due not later than 6 months after the end of the ELP’s fiscal year (e.g., for a 31 December year-end, filing is due 30 June of the following year).

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Relevant activity type: select any applicable activity (e.g., wholesale and retail distribution of goods from third parties).
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: A non-resident ELP that does not conduct relevant activities in Bermuda should state 'None' and remain outside ESR substance requirements.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Gross income from the relevant activity and gross income sourced outside Bermuda.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: If all income is derived from overseas sources and the ELP is managed abroad, it may be classified as a non-resident entity and file a simplified nil substance declaration.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Physical presence and employee data: number of full-time employees in Bermuda, monthly payroll costs, and square footage of business premises.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: A mere letterbox or wholly outsourced back-office structure may generate a substance deficiency; records of the ELP’s actual management and control location should be maintained.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Failure to file ESR-1: fixed penalty BMD 10,000 plus BMD 1,000 per day of continued non-compliance. False declaration: penalty of BMD 100,000 (first offence) and BMD 250,000 (subsequent offence); directors or general partners may be subject to imprisonment. Cancellation of the ELP’s registration can occur for persistent non-compliance.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 0% statutory withholding tax on dividends and partnership distributions. Bermuda does not impose corporate income tax, capital gains tax, or distribution withholding tax on profits repatriated to foreign partners.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: As Bermuda levies no withholding tax, treaty relief is generally unnecessary. Where a foreign jurisdiction imposes withholding on connection with amounts paid from or to Bermuda (e.g., UK, Gibraltar, or certain Caribbean states), a claim for treaty relief must be supported by (i) a valid Certificate of Tax Residency issued by the Bermuda Ministry of Finance, (ii) a completed claim form of the source-state tax authority, and (iii) a contemporaneous explanation of the partnership’s tax-transparent nature. If the ELP is a constituent entity of an MNE group, the GloBE IIR/UTPR charge may be relevant; the protocol requires submission of Form CIT-2 and the OECD standardised information return.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Bermuda imposes no withholding tax on cross-border royalty payments or debt interest. Applicable treaty rates in the rare context of a residence-based tax (e.g., under the Ireland-Bermuda unilateral exemption or Canada Trust Arrangement) are nil; the same documentary evidence as above must be retained.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: For Bermuda CIT purposes, a local file and master file are required where the combined group revenue equals or exceeds BMD 750 million (≈ EUR 750 million) and either: (i) related-party transactions in a fiscal year exceed BMD 1.5 million each, or (ii) aggregate related-party transactions exceed BMD 7.5 million. These thresholds mirror the OECD Transfer Pricing Guidelines and are the first applicable Bermuda TP documentation regime; a normal off-shore ELP wholesale operation will not meet these thresholds.
approved_arm_length_methodologies: CUP, Resale Price, Cost Plus, TNMM, Profit Split
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: The Bermuda Economic Substance Regulations apply to legal entities registered in Bermuda (including ELPs) that undertake any of the listed 'relevant activities'. Wholesale and retail distribution of goods from third parties is a relevant activity. However, a tax-transparent ELP that is not tax-resident in Bermuda and does not carry on the relevant activity from a fixed place in Bermuda may fall outside the substance requirements; it must still file an annual ESR declaration. Where the ELP has Bermuda management and is a 'registered entity', it must demonstrate economic substance by showing: (i) local generation and management of strategic decision-making, (ii) sufficient full-time employees, (iii) physical business premises, and (iv) annual operating expenditure proportionate to the value of the activity.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Deliberately omitting the ELP’s connection to a collective investment scheme or failing to disclose the ultimate beneficial owner of the ELP in the tax return or to the Registrar of Companies.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Under the Bermuda Tax Administration Act 2014, conviction for tax evasion carries a fine not exceeding BMD 100,000 and up to 5 years imprisonment; the partnership may be struck off and its assets forfeited.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: General partners of an ELP may be personally liable for restitution of evaded tax plus penalties; a travel ban and export order may be issued under the Proceeds of Crime Act; imprisonment up to 10 years for money laundering offences.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Shell Company / Lack of Economic Substance
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Using the ELP as a ‘brass plate’ nominee entity without any business purpose, staff, or premises in Bermuda, while claiming tax exemption on cross-border chip/SSD wholesale turnover.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: The Registrar may impose an economic substance fine of BMD 100,000 for the first offence and BMD 250,000 for subsequent offences; in egregious cases, the ELP is struck off and a declaration of non-compliance is published.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Each general partner is jointly and severally liable for the penalties; the court may order disqualification from acting as a partner or director for up to 5 years; personal breach of ESR duty may attract a separate fine and up to 1 year imprisonment.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Failure to conduct adequate customer due diligence and beneficial-ownership checks on counterparties involved in flash-memory CPU chip trades, which often serve as high-volume instruments for trade-based money laundering.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Under the Proceeds of Crime (Anti-Money Laundering) Regulations 2008, the Financial Intelligence Agency can impose a civil penalty up to BMD 250,000 per violation; criminal conviction carries a fine and imprisonment up to 7 years.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors and the general partner’s compliance officer assume direct personal liability; failure to file a Suspicious Activity Report can lead to custodial sentences of up to 2 years and a permanent ban from holding a licence under the Trust or Company Service Providers Act.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Misapplication of Treaty Relief / False Compliance Statement
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Certifying a false tax residency of the ELP (e.g., claiming UK FTSE legal residence) to suppress foreign withholding tax on royalty income derived from IP-related chip designs, without any management or control being exercised in the UK.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: A false statement made to a foreign tax authority constitutes fraud at common law and a breach of the Bermuda Criminal Code; penalties include an unlimited fine, seizure of assets, and extradition agreements enabling prosecution in the country of the treaty abuse.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Any signatory partner of the ELP who knowingly makes a false declaration is criminally liable; civil remedies include recovery of all unpaid withholding taxes, interest at 2% monthly, and a court order freezing personal bank accounts; imprisonment of up to 7 years may also be imposed.
